title: Create and Edit Files in Harvey
format_note: One prompt, three outputs (Word memo, Excel model, PowerPoint deck) shown in a 54 s music-only film with a single hard cut before the end card.
one_thing: One long legal prompt becomes three finished Office files without leaving Harvey.

transcript.voice_style: No speech. Captions report only [music] tags and a stray '>> Mhm.' at 53 s.
transcript.script_shape: All meaning is on-screen text: wordmark, feature title, typed prompt, three highlighted verbs, three product demos, recap, tagline, availability line, end card.

structure.first_3s: Wordmark at 0.33 s, then a white/grey split with the headline 'Create and Edit Files' and Word, Excel, PowerPoint icons sliding in from 2.1 s (strips/window-03-2.133s.jpg).

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: One shot runs 0 to 49.47 s (0.917 of runtime). Change comes from UI state: panels slide, logs type, chips tick. Median hold between changes 1.33 s, longest static run 4 s (metrics.json).

look.accent_use: No brand accent. Colour comes only from the three Office icons and the output files themselves; the check ticks are soft green.
look.type: Serif wordmark and serif closing lines; geometric grotesque bold for 'Create and Edit Files' and chips; small sans for the Answering log.
look.depth: Flat. Soft drop shadow on white chips and panels; no parallax or 3D; panels slide on one plane.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: No zoom or pan. The UI sits in a fixed right pane; the film cross-fades its content (log, skeleton, file) at one position.
product_ui.notes: Prompt text is about 1.9 % of frame height and the Answering log about 1.6 %, so both need the zoom-free eye of a desktop. File names and the spreadsheet title are legible. The three highlighted phrases carry the message.

motion.text_entry: Prompt types at a cursor; end lines fade word by word over about 0.15 to 0.3 s per word; phrases sit at slightly different offsets, then lift into rows.
motion.ui_motion: Right pane content swaps: log lines fade in and scroll up, skeleton resolves to the real file, grid cells fill top to bottom, deck thumbnails scroll sideways as 'Generating Deck...'.
motion.camera: Static. All movement is panels and elements.
motion.eases: Soft ease-out slides and fades; no overshoot visible in strips. Exit of the right pane at 42.3 to 42.9 s is about 0.6 s against a longer build-in.

good.observation: Three verbs from the prompt are highlighted black while the rest greys out, then lift into rows paired with app chips, so a 60-word prompt becomes three readable ideas.
good.evidence: f0005.jpg at 8 s, f0006.jpg at 10 s

good.observation: One fixed left chip with a spinner turning into a green tick tells task state while the right pane runs log, skeleton, result; the same grammar repeats for all three apps.
The recap at 43 s reuses the exact chip-and-phrase layout from 11 s, closing the loop before the tagline.
Outputs are shown as real, specific files (Crestview V memos, a ten-LP fee table with TOTAL, a navy deck with 10/84/7/5 stats), which proves the claim better than a generic mock.
Large quiet end lines: serif 'Available in Early Access' at 8.8 % height with word-by-word fade, then a dark card with tagline held 4.4 s.
Disciplined palette: white and warm grey, with colour supplied only by the three Office icons and the files themselves.

weak.observation: Typed prompt (about 1.9 % of frame height) and the Answering log (about 1.6 %) sit below the 2.6 % legibility floor, and memo body text is unreadable at 1280 px.
Left half of the frame holds only a small chip for 27 s (14 to 41 s), so the product pane is roughly 40 % of width and the pane's content is small.
No cut lands on a musical onset and the single hard cut sits at 49.47 s, so picture and music feel unconnected.
True peak -0.6 dBTP exceeds the -1 dBTP ceiling for social masters.

rule_candidates.rule: A film can open on a blank frame and a lone serif wordmark at 0.33 s if the feature title and product follow by 2.1 s; the film still landed its hook inside 3 s.
A single continuous shot (91.7 % of runtime, one hard cut) can carry a feature demo if UI state changes every 1 to 3 s; use it when the product is the subject.
Hold a persistent status chip on one side (spinner, then tick) and swap the demo content on the other side; repeat the identical layout for each feature so state reads at a glance.
Condense a long on-screen paragraph by greying it out and leaving 3 key phrases black for 2.6 s, then lift those phrases into the next layout.
Repeat an early layout as a recap just before the tagline (here 10.7 s then 43 s) so the viewer re-reads the claim without new copy.
End on a last line held well beyond the floor: here 4.4 s, 2.2 times the 2 s minimum, after a 1.8 s availability line faded in word by word.
Ship at -14 LUFS but check true peak: this film measures -14.0 LUFS and -0.6 dBTP, which breaks the -1 dBTP ceiling.
Quiet monochrome ground with colour only from product icons and outputs; a pale background and no accent still reads as premium and keeps focus on the demo.
